title: Self-Aug: Query and Entropy Adaptive Decoding for Large Vision-Language Models
claim: A query-aware augmentation is chosen by the model itself, then an entropy-adaptive threshold truncates candidates when contrasting original and augmented outputs.
layout: 2 boxed panels, left-to-right, frozen-model icons with bar charts at right
description: Two rounded boxes side by side show the two stages of the method. The left box, titled Self-Augmentation Selection Prompting, has a gray text box holding the instruction prompt and the query 'What color is the coat?'. An arrow leads into a gray trapezoid labeled LVLM with a snowflake (frozen) icon. The model outputs a 'Choice: Color inversion.' bubble. That choice is applied to the original skier photo to give a color-inverted 'Contrasted image'. The right box, titled Sparsity Adaptive Truncation, feeds both images and the question through the LVLM. Each pass produces a horizontal bar chart over Red, Cyan and Pink: maroon for the original, yellow for the contrasted image. A dashed threshold line labeled β^SAT truncates the candidates. The final sample step over the surviving tokens gives 'Red'. Gray arrows guide the left-to-right flow.
caption: Overview of the proposed augmentation choice process and sparsity adaptive truncation.
abstract: Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) have demonstrated remarkable multimodal capabilities, but they inherit the tendency to hallucinate from their underlying language models. While visual contrastive decoding has been proposed to mitigate this issue, existing methods often apply generic visual augmentations that disregard the specific context provided by the text query, limiting their effectiveness. This study introduces a novel training-free decoding strategy that addresses these limitations, featuring two key contributions. First, a self-augmentation prompting strategy that leverages the intrinsic knowledge of the model to dynamically align semantics between the query and the visual augmentation. Second, an adaptive thresholding algorithm that adaptively adjusts next token candidate size based on the output sparsity, utilizing full information from the logit distribution. Extensive experiments across four LVLMs and seven benchmarks demonstrate that the proposed decoding significantly enhances factual consistency compared to state-of-the-art decoding methods. This work highlights the importance of integrating query-dependent augmentation and entropy-aware decoding for improving effective generation of LVLMs.
